outline.h2: The Short Answer: Dry Rot vs Termites in 90 Seconds
outline.notes: Lead with the two-sentence differentiator. Dry rot = fungal, cubical/cracked wood, musty smell, no insects visible. Termites = insect damage, hollow sound, mud tubes, visible wings or frass. Both common in Bay Area; often co-occur.

outline.h2: What's Dry Rot and What Are Termites? (The 60-Second Biology)
outline.notes: Short primer. Dry rot = wood-decay fungi needing 20%+ moisture content. Termites = insects (subterranean + drywood species common in Bay Area). Both eat wood but by different mechanisms.

outline.h2: How to Tell Dry Rot and Termite Damage Apart
h3: Visual Pattern: Cubical Cracking vs Hollow Galleries
Smell: Musty vs No Odor
Debris: Fungal Strands vs Frass (Insect Pellets)
Mud Tubes and Wings: Termite Dead Giveaways
The Screwdriver Test (Works for Both)
outline.notes: Diagnostic grid. Specific tells for each. Frass looks like coffee grounds / sawdust pellets. Mud tubes = subterranean termites. Discarded wings near windows = swarming drywood termites.

outline.h2: Where Each Hides in Bay Area Homes
h3: Dry Rot Hotspots: Fog Belt Window Sills, Deck Ledgers, Bay Window Bases
Subterranean Termite Hotspots: Foundation-Adjacent Wood, Crawl Space, Earth-to-Wood Contact
Drywood Termite Hotspots: Attic Rafters, Fascia, Door Jambs, Window Frames
outline.notes: Hyper-local. Subterranean termites in East Bay and Peninsula clay soils. Drywood termites throughout. Dry rot concentrated in coastal fog belt (Sunset, Pacifica, Daly City, Sausalito).

outline.h2: What If You Have Both? (It's Common)
outline.notes: Termite-damaged wood with chronic moisture also develops dry rot. Order of operations: pest control treats termites first, then structural contractor removes damaged wood, fixes water source, replaces framing. Explain scope boundary between pest control and general contractor.

outline.h2: What Dry Rot Repair Costs (Our Scope)
outline.notes: Localized $800–$2,500; whole-wall $4,000–$12,000; structural $12,000–$30,000+. Cross-link to the dry rot post for depth.

outline.h2: What Termite Damage Repair Costs (After Pest Control Does Their Part)
outline.notes: Explicit: pest control treats the infestation ($800–$3,000 typical), then structural repair of damaged framing is our scope. Repair ranges: localized trim/sill $600–$2,000; joist/beam replacement $3,500–$15,000; major structural $15,000–$45,000+.

outline.h2: When to Call a Pest Inspector vs a General Contractor
outline.notes: Decision framework. Suspect termites (frass, wings, mud tubes) → pest inspector first. Suspect dry rot (musty smell, fungal strands, soft wood near water source) → general contractor. Both → sequence pest first, then structural.
